title: Calculus II
subject: Mathematics

cards.prompt: Define antiderivative verification by differentiation.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The differentiation and domain check that independently verifies a proposed indefinite integral.
required_concepts: The differentiation and domain check that independently verifies a proposed indefinite integral.
major_error_concepts: Checking only that the expression resembles the integration-by-parts template.

cards.prompt: Define Cyclic integration-by-parts equation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An integration-by-parts calculation in which the original integral returns and must be algebraically isolated.
required_concepts: An integration-by-parts calculation in which the original integral returns and must be algebraically isolated.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every returned-integral equation has the same coefficient, or canceling unequal integral terms instead of collecting and algebraically isolating the original integral when possible.

cards.prompt: Define Definite integration by parts. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The parts identity with boundary evaluation uv evaluated from a to b and a definite residual integral.
required_concepts: The parts identity with boundary evaluation uv evaluated from a to b and a definite residual integral.
major_error_concepts: Adding an arbitrary constant to a definite result.

cards.prompt: Define Elementary substitution review. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: Substitution reverses the chain rule: with u=g(x), du=g'(x)dx, so integral f(g(x))g'(x)dx becomes integral f(u)du. Transform the integrand and differential consistently; for definite integrals transform bounds or return to the original variable before evaluation. A different correct method is not an error merely because it is less efficient.
required_concepts: Match a derivative factor with the chosen inner variable.
Transform both integrand and differential consistently.
Use bounds matching the variable in a definite integral.
accepted_variants: Use u=g(x) and du=g'(x)dx so the whole integral transforms consistently. Integration by parts can also be valid; choosing it is not by itself a mathematical error.
major_error_concepts: Set u=g(x) but leave dx unchanged and drop the factor g'(x).

cards.prompt: Define Integration-by-parts identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The antiderivative identity integral u dv=uv-integral v du derived from the product rule.
required_concepts: The antiderivative identity integral u dv=uv-integral v du derived from the product rule.
major_error_concepts: Writing uv+integral vdu and reversing the sign.

cards.prompt: Define Integration-strategy stop rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The condition that ends symbolic manipulation when the result is verified, the residual is strictly simpler, or a bounded nonelementary interface is justified.
required_concepts: The condition that ends symbolic manipulation when the result is verified, the residual is strictly simpler, or a bounded nonelementary interface is justified.
major_error_concepts: Continuing transformations after verification and introducing avoidable algebra errors.

cards.prompt: Define Nonelementary-antiderivative recognition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The qualified conclusion that a method inventory does not produce an elementary antiderivative, without claiming the definite integral or function is meaningless.
required_concepts: The available method inventory does not produce an elementary antiderivative for the integrand.
This conclusion does not make the underlying function or a corresponding definite integral meaningless.
major_error_concepts: Inventing an antiderivative by dividing a composite expression by a nonconstant inner derivative as though that divisor were constant, without differentiating the candidate to verify it.

cards.prompt: Define Parts factor-selection criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The choice of u and dv that makes du simpler and v computable while decreasing a declared complexity measure.
required_concepts: The choice of u and dv that makes du simpler and v computable while decreasing a declared complexity measure.
major_error_concepts: Claiming a factor choice guarantees simplification without checking that v is computable and that the remaining integral improves under the declared complexity criterion.

cards.prompt: Define Reduction identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A recurrence expressing an indexed integral in terms of a lower-index case plus boundary terms, with a base case.
required_concepts: A recurrence expressing an indexed integral in terms of a lower-index case plus boundary terms, with a base case.
major_error_concepts: Using the recurrence without recording its base case or index range.

cards.prompt: Define Repeated integration by parts. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** successive valid applications used when one differentiated factor simplifies in stages.
required_concepts: successive valid applications used when one differentiated factor simplifies in stages.
major_error_concepts: Declaring an explicit evaluation complete while the intended unresolved integral still remains, when further valid integration-by-parts steps are needed.

cards.prompt: Define Tabular integration by parts. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A bookkeeping form for repeated parts when derivatives terminate and antiderivatives remain simple.
required_concepts: A bookkeeping form for repeated parts when derivatives terminate and antiderivatives remain simple.
major_error_concepts: Losing the alternating sign pattern.

cards.prompt: Define Distinct-linear partial fractions. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The complete decomposition template for a proper rational function with distinct linear denominator factors.
required_concepts: The complete decomposition template for a proper rational function with distinct linear denominator factors.
major_error_concepts: Using one constant over the full product and calling it a decomposition.

cards.prompt: Define Even sine-cosine power reduction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The half-angle reduction used when both sine and cosine powers are even.
required_concepts: The half-angle reduction used when both sine and cosine powers are even.
major_error_concepts: Dropping the factor 1/2 or doubled angle in the half-angle identities used to reduce even sine/cosine powers.

cards.prompt: Define Irreducible-quadratic partial fractions. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: For each power of a real irreducible quadratic factor in a partial-fraction decomposition, use a general numerator of degree at most one, Ax+B. Determine the coefficients from the rational-function identity; A may be zero, so a constant numerator is valid when the coefficient solution gives one.
required_concepts: Allow a numerator Ax+B of degree at most one at every relevant irreducible-quadratic power; A may be zero in a valid special case.
major_error_concepts: Restricting every irreducible-quadratic numerator to a constant instead of allowing Ax+B at each repeated power; A may be zero when the coefficient solution warrants it.

cards.prompt: Define Partial-fraction coefficient verification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: After clearing denominators, verify that the proposed numerator identity holds. Comparing every coefficient is sufficient. Evaluating at d+1 distinct points is also sufficient when the difference is known to have degree at most d. A smaller set of convenient points alone does not generally establish the identity.
required_concepts: Clear denominators to obtain a polynomial identity.
Verify all coefficients or enough distinct values for the known degree bound.
Too few sample values do not prove the identity.
accepted_variants: For a difference polynomial of degree at most two, agreement at three distinct points proves it is zero; full coefficient comparison is an alternative.
major_error_concepts: Agreement at two sample points proves any polynomial identity, regardless of its degree.

cards.prompt: Define proper rational function criterion.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The degree comparison requiring polynomial division before partial fractions when numerator degree is not smaller.
required_concepts: The degree comparison requiring polynomial division before partial fractions when numerator degree is not smaller.
major_error_concepts: Starting partial fractions directly on an improper rational function.

cards.prompt: Define Repeated-linear partial fractions. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement for one term at every power of a repeated linear factor.
required_concepts: The requirement for one term at every power of a repeated linear factor.
major_error_concepts: Omitting the first-power repeated-factor term.

cards.prompt: Define Secant trigonometric substitution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The substitution x=a sec theta for radicals sqrt(x^2-a^2), with interval-dependent absolute values.
required_concepts: The substitution x=a sec theta for radicals sqrt(x^2-a^2), with interval-dependent absolute values.
major_error_concepts: Dropping abs(sec theta) without restricting x and theta.

cards.prompt: Describe the usual parity strategies for integrating sin^m x cos^n x with nonnegative integer powers.
cards.definition: For integral sin^m(x)cos^n(x)dx with nonnegative integer powers, if m is odd, save sin x dx and rewrite the remaining even sine power using 1-cos^2 x, then set u=cos x. If n is odd, save cos x dx and use u=sin x. If both powers are even, half-angle identities reduce powers. These are efficient choices, not the only valid methods.
required_concepts: Odd sine power supports saving sin x dx and substituting cos x.
Odd cosine power supports saving cos x dx and substituting sin x.
For both even powers, use half-angle reduction; other correct routes remain acceptable.
major_error_concepts: Set u=cos x and replace du by cos x dx.

cards.prompt: Define Sine trigonometric substitution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The substitution x=a sin theta for radicals sqrt(a^2-x^2), with branch and back-substitution control.
required_concepts: The substitution x=a sin theta for radicals sqrt(a^2-x^2), with branch and back-substitution control.
major_error_concepts: Returning from theta with an unsigned triangle relation that ignores the selected inverse branch.

cards.prompt: State the common tangent-secant parity substitutions and when each derivative factor is available.
cards.definition: For integral tan^m(x)sec^n(x)dx with nonnegative integer powers, an even secant power n≥2 lets you save sec^2 x dx, use sec^2 x=1+tan^2 x, and set u=tan x. If m is odd and n≥1, saving sec x tan x dx can support u=sec x and tan^2 x=sec^2 x-1. These are sufficient strategies; valid alternatives are allowed.
required_concepts: An even secant power can supply the derivative sec^2 x for u=tan x.
An odd tangent power with a secant factor can supply sec x tan x for u=sec x.
Identities and differentials must stay valid; inefficiency alone is not an error.
major_error_concepts: Use u=sec x with du=sec^2 x dx.

cards.prompt: Define Tangent trigonometric substitution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The substitution x=a tan theta for radicals sqrt(a^2+x^2).
required_concepts: The substitution x=a tan theta for radicals sqrt(a^2+x^2).
major_error_concepts: Using a trigonometric identity or branch simplification inconsistent with x=a tan(theta), such as replacing sqrt(1+tan^2(theta)) by tan(theta).

cards.prompt: Define trigonometric identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A trigonometric identity is an equality between trigonometric expressions that holds for every input in their common domain and may therefore transform an integrand without changing its value there.
required_concepts: A trigonometric identity is an equality between trigonometric expressions that holds for every input in their common domain.
Such an identity can transform an integrand without changing its value on that domain.
major_error_concepts: Using a sign, factor, or domain-restricted relation that does not give an identity on the domain of integration.

cards.term: Absolute convergence of an improper integral
cards.prompt: Define Absolute convergence of an improper integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The finiteness of the integral of abs(f), which implies convergence of the signed improper integral.
required_concepts: The finiteness of the integral of abs(f), which implies convergence of the signed improper integral.
major_error_concepts: Showing only cancellation of positive and negative lobes.

cards.prompt: Define Composite midpoint rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The sum of function values at subinterval midpoints times a common step size on a regular partition.
required_concepts: The sum of function values at subinterval midpoints times a common step size on a regular partition.
major_error_concepts: Using endpoints while labeling the result midpoint.

cards.prompt: Define Composite Simpson rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The h/3 weighted rule with pattern 1,4,2,...,4,1 and an even number of equal subintervals.
required_concepts: The h/3 weighted rule with pattern 1,4,2,...,4,1 and an even number of equal subintervals.
major_error_concepts: Applying Simpson with an odd subinterval count.

cards.prompt: Define Composite trapezoid rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The weighted endpoint-and-interior sum h[half f(a)+interior values+half f(b)].
required_concepts: The weighted endpoint-and-interior sum h[half f(a)+interior values+half f(b)].
major_error_concepts: Using full interior weight for both endpoint samples in the composite trapezoid sum instead of the required half endpoint weights.

cards.prompt: Define Direct comparison for improper integrals. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The nonnegative-function bound transferring convergence from an upper comparator or divergence from a lower comparator.
required_concepts: The nonnegative-function bound transferring convergence from an upper comparator or divergence from a lower comparator.
major_error_concepts: Bounding above by divergent 1/x and claiming convergence.

cards.prompt: Define Endpoint-singularity improper integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The one-sided limit of proper integrals approaching an endpoint where the integrand is unbounded or undefined.
required_concepts: The one-sided limit of proper integrals approaching an endpoint where the integrand is unbounded or undefined.
major_error_concepts: Substituting directly at the singular endpoint instead of forming the required one-sided limit of proper integrals.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Improper convergence versus value.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between proving a finite defining limit exists and then identifying its numerical value.
required_concepts: Convergence means that the defining improper limit exists as a finite real number.
The value of the improper integral is the numerical value of that finite limit.
A formal antiderivative expression does not establish a value until the defining limit has been shown to converge.
major_error_concepts: Computing an antiderivative expression and omitting the convergence statement.

cards.term: improper integral with an interior singularity
cards.prompt: Define improper integral with an interior singularity.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement to split at every interior singularity and demand finite convergence of each one-sided piece.
required_concepts: The requirement to split at every interior singularity and demand finite convergence of each one-sided piece.
major_error_concepts: Cancelling symmetric areas and reporting zero as the ordinary improper integral.

cards.prompt: Define Infinite-endpoint improper integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The limit of proper integrals over expanding finite bounds, with convergence requiring a finite limit.
required_concepts: The limit of proper integrals over expanding finite bounds, with convergence requiring a finite limit.
major_error_concepts: Writing infinity as an endpoint and substituting it into the antiderivative as a real number.

cards.prompt: Define Infinite-range p-integral criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The convergence of integral_1^infinity x^(-p) dx exactly when p>1.
required_concepts: The convergence of integral_1^infinity x^(-p) dx exactly when p>1.
major_error_concepts: Using the near-zero p criterion and reversing the inequality.

cards.prompt: Define Limit comparison for improper integrals. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The positive finite asymptotic ratio that transfers convergence behavior between nonnegative integrands.
required_concepts: The positive finite asymptotic ratio that transfers convergence behavior between nonnegative integrands.
major_error_concepts: Using a ratio limit of zero or infinity as though it were the positive-finite theorem without extra reasoning.

cards.prompt: Define Near-zero p-integral criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The convergence of integral_0^1 x^(-p) dx exactly when p<1.
required_concepts: The convergence of integral_0^1 x^(-p) dx exactly when p<1.
major_error_concepts: Using the infinite-range criterion p>1 at a finite singularity.

cards.prompt: Define Numerical-integration tolerance plan. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The selection of rule and step count from assumptions and an error bound, followed by an a posteriori plausibility check.
required_concepts: The selection of rule and step count from assumptions and an error bound, followed by an a posteriori plausibility check.
major_error_concepts: Increasing n until displayed digits stabilize and calling that a proof without an error contract.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Quadrature error versus bound.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The actual difference between estimate and exact integral separated from a theorem-derived maximum using derivative bounds.
required_concepts: Actual quadrature error is the difference between the numerical estimate and the exact integral.
An error bound is a theorem-derived maximum obtained from hypotheses such as a derivative bound.
The theoretical bound need not equal the actual error; it only limits its magnitude when the hypotheses hold.
major_error_concepts: Calling the theoretical upper bound the observed error.

cards.prompt: Define Quadrature exactness class. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The polynomial-degree class integrated exactly by a rule under its partition assumptions.
required_concepts: The polynomial-degree class integrated exactly by a rule under its partition assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Claiming Simpson is exact for every smooth function.

cards.prompt: Define center-of-mass formula.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The paired accumulations M=integral rho(x)dx and M_1=integral x rho(x)dx over identical bounds and density units before their ratio locates a center of mass.
required_concepts: The paired accumulations M=integral rho(x)dx and M_1=integral x rho(x)dx over identical bounds and density units before their ratio locates a center of mass.
major_error_concepts: Computing mass and moment from different bounds or density specifications and then dividing them.

cards.prompt: Define dimensional consistency of an integral.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The reconciliation of integrand units, differential units, and final quantity before accepting a physical integral.
required_concepts: The reconciliation of integrand units, differential units, and final quantity before accepting a physical integral.
major_error_concepts: Dropping dy units and accepting a result with pressure units.

cards.prompt: Define First moment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The signed density-weighted position integral used with total mass to locate a center of mass.
required_concepts: The signed density-weighted position integral used with total mass to locate a center of mass.
major_error_concepts: Dividing by mass inside the moment definition.

cards.prompt: Define Fluid-pressure law. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** pressure equal to weight density times depth below a fluid surface under the model assumptions.
required_concepts: pressure equal to weight density times depth below a fluid surface under the model assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Using total depth for every slice.

cards.prompt: Define Geometric-physical sanity bound. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An independent containment symmetry positivity or constant-case check on an arc surface force mass or centroid result.
required_concepts: An independent containment symmetry positivity or constant-case check on an arc surface force mass or centroid result.
major_error_concepts: Trusting exact symbolic algebra despite violating a geometric bound.

cards.prompt: Define Graph arc-length differential. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The limiting segment length ds=sqrt(1+[f'(x)]^2)dx derived from local right triangles for a smooth graph.
required_concepts: The limiting segment length ds=sqrt(1+[f'(x)]^2)dx derived from local right triangles for a smooth graph.
major_error_concepts: Using integral f(x)dx as curve length.

cards.prompt: Define Graph arc-length integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The definite integral of the nonnegative arc-length differential over the parameter interval.
required_concepts: The definite integral of the nonnegative arc-length differential over the parameter interval.
major_error_concepts: Allowing a negative length after reversing bounds without an orientation convention.

cards.prompt: Define Hydrostatic-force slice. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The product pressure times the area of a thin submerged strip, integrated over depth.
required_concepts: The product pressure times the area of a thin submerged strip, integrated over depth.
major_error_concepts: Multiplying maximum pressure wH by total area and ignoring variation.

cards.prompt: Define One-dimensional center of mass. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The first moment divided by positive total mass when both integrals exist.
required_concepts: The first moment divided by positive total mass when both integrals exist.
major_error_concepts: Averaging endpoints for a nonuniform rod without checking density.

cards.prompt: How do planar geometric centroid formulas differ from center-of-mass formulas for nonuniform density?
cards.definition: For a planar region R with positive finite area A and finite absolute first area moments, its geometric centroid is xbar=(1/A) integral_R x dA and ybar=(1/A) integral_R y dA. For a lamina with nonnegative density rho, its center of mass uses M=integral_R rho dA and density-weighted moments divided by M, requiring 0<M<infinity and finite absolute first density-weighted moments. Geometric centroid and center of mass coincide for uniform positive density whenever these quantities exist.
required_concepts: A geometric centroid uses finite area moments divided by positive finite area.
Nonuniform center of mass uses finite density-weighted moments divided by positive finite total mass.
Uniform positive density makes the two coincide when the moments exist.
major_error_concepts: For any nonuniform density, divide the density-weighted moment by geometric area to get the center of mass.

cards.prompt: Define radius of rotation.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The perpendicular distance from the curve to the rotation axis, which may be f(x), x, or an offset.
required_concepts: The perpendicular distance from the curve to the rotation axis, which may be f(x), x, or an offset.
major_error_concepts: Using a coordinate or curve height as the rotation radius without measuring perpendicular distance to the stated axis, including any offset.

cards.prompt: Define Surface-of-revolution differential. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The local lateral-area element 2pi(radius)ds with radius measured to the axis of rotation.
required_concepts: The local lateral-area element 2pi(radius)ds with radius measured to the axis of rotation.
major_error_concepts: Using disk area pi x^2 dx, which computes volume rather than surface area.

cards.prompt: Define Bounded sequence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A sequence whose terms remain between fixed finite lower and upper bounds independent of n.
required_concepts: A sequence whose terms remain between fixed finite lower and upper bounds independent of n.
major_error_concepts: Claiming boundedness implies convergence.

cards.prompt: Define Explicit sequence formula. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A rule computing a_n directly from n without earlier terms.
required_concepts: A rule computing a_n directly from n without earlier terms.
major_error_concepts: Starting the index at zero without checking the declared convention.

cards.prompt: Define Infinite sequence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A function from positive integers to values whose ordered terms retain their index identity.
required_concepts: A function from positive integers to values whose ordered terms retain their index identity.
major_error_concepts: Treating the sequence as an unordered set and losing repeated or indexed terms.

cards.term: Monotone convergence theorem for sequences: role
cards.prompt: What is Monotone convergence theorem for sequences used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It certifies convergence without first knowing the limit whenever a real sequence is both monotone and bounded; it gives existence, not a convergence rate or the limit's value.
required_concepts: It certifies convergence without first knowing the limit whenever a real sequence is both monotone and bounded
it gives existence, not a convergence rate or the limit's value.
major_error_concepts: Using the theorem when monotonicity begins to fail infinitely often.

cards.prompt: State Monotone convergence theorem for sequences, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** The first-course theorem that every bounded monotone real sequence converges.
required_concepts: The real sequence is monotone.
The sequence is bounded.
The sequence converges to a finite real limit.
major_error_concepts: Using the theorem when monotonicity begins to fail infinitely often.

cards.prompt: Define Monotone sequence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A sequence that is nondecreasing or nonincreasing for every successive index in its declared range.
required_concepts: A sequence that is nondecreasing or nonincreasing for every successive index in its declared range.
major_error_concepts: Checking only the first few differences.

cards.prompt: Define Recursive fixed-point candidate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A value L satisfying L=g(L) that any convergent recurrence a_{n+1}=g(a_n) may approach when limit passage is valid.
required_concepts: A value L satisfying L=g(L) that any convergent recurrence a_{n+1}=g(a_n) may approach when limit passage is valid.
major_error_concepts: Calling the fixed point the limit without proving convergence.

cards.prompt: Define recursively defined sequence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A recursively defined sequence is specified by enough initial values together with a recurrence that uniquely determines every later indexed term in its stated range.
required_concepts: A recursively defined sequence includes enough initial values to start the recurrence.
Its recurrence uniquely determines every later indexed term in the stated range.
major_error_concepts: Using the recurrence without the initial data needed to determine a unique sequence.

cards.prompt: Define Sequence convergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The epsilon-tail property that all sufficiently late terms lie within epsilon of one finite limit.
required_concepts: The epsilon-tail property that all sufficiently late terms lie within epsilon of one finite limit.
major_error_concepts: Checking only many finite terms and calling the observed pattern proof.

cards.prompt: Define Sequence divergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** failure to approach any single finite limit, established by unboundedness oscillation or separated subsequences.
required_concepts: failure to approach any single finite limit, established by unboundedness oscillation or separated subsequences.
major_error_concepts: Averaging oscillating values to claim limit zero.

cards.prompt: Define sequence limit laws.
cards.definition: **Definition.** sum product quotient and continuous-function limit laws used only when component limits and denominator conditions hold.
required_concepts: sum product quotient and continuous-function limit laws used only when component limits and denominator conditions hold.
major_error_concepts: Applying quotient algebra when the denominator limit is zero.

cards.prompt: What is Sequence squeeze theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It proves convergence of a difficult sequence by trapping it between two sequences with one common limit; boundedness alone or bounds with different limits are insufficient.
required_concepts: It proves convergence of a difficult sequence by trapping it between two sequences with one common limit
boundedness alone or bounds with different limits are insufficient.
major_error_concepts: Bounding sin n but forgetting division by n.

cards.prompt: State Sequence squeeze theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If a_n<=b_n<=c_n eventually and a_n and c_n both converge to L, then b_n converges to L.
required_concepts: The eventual bounds a_n<=b_n<=c_n hold.
Both bounding sequences converge to the same limit L.
The trapped sequence b_n converges to L.
major_error_concepts: Bounding sin n but forgetting division by n.

cards.prompt: Define Subsequence witness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A sequence formed from strictly increasing indices, used to preserve or separate limiting behavior.
required_concepts: A sequence formed from strictly increasing indices, used to preserve or separate limiting behavior.
major_error_concepts: Selecting indices that are not strictly increasing.

cards.prompt: Define Absolute convergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** convergence of sum abs(a_n), which implies convergence of sum a_n.
required_concepts: convergence of sum abs(a_n), which implies convergence of sum a_n.
major_error_concepts: Testing only the signed series and assuming absolute convergence.

cards.prompt: Define Alternating-series remainder bound. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The bound abs(R_N)<=b_{N+1} when the alternating-series hypotheses hold.
required_concepts: The bound abs(R_N)<=b_{N+1} when the alternating-series hypotheses hold.
major_error_concepts: Using the next-term bound for a nonmonotone alternating magnitude.

cards.prompt: Define Alternating-series test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The convergence result for decreasing magnitudes tending to zero with alternating signs.
required_concepts: The convergence result for decreasing magnitudes tending to zero with alternating signs.
major_error_concepts: Claiming absolute convergence from the alternating test.

cards.prompt: Define Conditional convergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** convergence of a signed series together with divergence of its absolute-value series.
required_concepts: convergence of a signed series together with divergence of its absolute-value series.
major_error_concepts: Calling every alternating convergent series conditionally convergent without testing absolute values.

cards.prompt: Define Direct comparison test for series. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The transfer of convergence from a larger nonnegative series or divergence from a smaller nonnegative series.
required_concepts: The transfer of convergence from a larger nonnegative series or divergence from a smaller nonnegative series.
major_error_concepts: Bounding it above by divergent 1/n and claiming convergence.

cards.prompt: State the sum and convergence condition for sum from n=0 to infinity of a r^n, including the zero-series exception.
cards.definition: For the series sum from n=0 to infinity of a r^n, if a≠0 it converges exactly when |r|<1 and then equals a/(1-r). If a=0, every term is zero and the series converges to zero for every finite real or complex r. A different starting index changes the first term and therefore the numerator.
required_concepts: Specify the start n=0 and sum a/(1-r).
For nonzero a, convergence is equivalent to |r|<1.
The all-zero series is a trivial exception.
major_error_concepts: The nonzero series sum from n=0 of 2^n converges to -1 by a/(1-r).

cards.prompt: What claim does Harmonic-series counterexample refute, and why?
cards.definition: **Definition.** The harmonic series sum from n=1 to infinity of 1/n refutes the claim that a_n tending to zero is sufficient for sum a_n to converge. Its terms satisfy 1/n to 0, but its partial sums diverge without bound.
required_concepts: The false claim is that a_n tending to zero is sufficient for the series sum a_n to converge.
The concrete witness is the harmonic series sum from n=1 to infinity of 1/n.
Its terms satisfy 1/n tending to zero.
Its partial sums diverge without bound, so the series does not converge.
major_error_concepts: Calling slow numerical growth evidence of convergence.

cards.prompt: Define Infinite series as partial-sum limit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The sum of a series defined as the finite limit of its sequence of partial sums, not as direct addition of infinitely many terms.
required_concepts: The sum of a series defined as the finite limit of its sequence of partial sums, not as direct addition of infinitely many terms.
major_error_concepts: Checking only that a_n->0.

cards.prompt: State the integral-test upper and lower bounds for the remainder after N terms.
cards.definition: If f is positive, continuous, and decreasing on a tail, a_n=f(n), and the series converges, its tail R_N=sum from n=N+1 to infinity of a_n satisfies integral from N+1 to infinity of f(x)dx ≤ R_N ≤ integral from N to infinity of f(x)dx. Choose N within the region where the assumptions hold.
required_concepts: The remainder starts after the Nth term.
Lower integral starts at N+1; upper integral starts at N.
Use a positive continuous decreasing tail and convergence.
major_error_concepts: The tail R_N lies above integral from N to infinity and below integral from N+1 to infinity.

cards.prompt: Define Integral test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The shared convergence of a positive continuous decreasing f and sum f(n) with assumptions checked on a tail.
required_concepts: The shared convergence of a positive continuous decreasing f and sum f(n) with assumptions checked on a tail.
major_error_concepts: Applying the test to a sign-changing sequence without modification.

cards.prompt: Define Limit comparison test for series. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The positive finite term ratio transferring convergence behavior between positive series.
required_concepts: The positive finite term ratio transferring convergence behavior between positive series.
major_error_concepts: Using a ratio limit of zero as the stated positive-finite theorem without an additional comparison.

cards.prompt: Define Nth-term divergence test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The one-way result that a series diverges when its terms fail to approach zero.
required_concepts: The one-way result that a series diverges when its terms fail to approach zero.
major_error_concepts: Claiming convergence whenever terms approach zero.

cards.prompt: Define p-series criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The convergence of sum 1/n^p exactly when p>1.
required_concepts: The convergence of sum 1/n^p exactly when p>1.
major_error_concepts: Using the near-zero improper-integral inequality instead.

cards.prompt: Define Ratio test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The limit of abs(a_{n+1}/a_n), giving absolute convergence below 1 divergence above 1 and no conclusion at 1.
required_concepts: The limit of abs(a_{n+1}/a_n), giving absolute convergence below 1 divergence above 1 and no conclusion at 1.
major_error_concepts: Forgetting the absolute value or claiming convergence when the ratio limit is 1.

cards.prompt: Define Root test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The limsup of the nth root of abs(a_n), with the same below-one above-one inconclusive-one trichotomy.
required_concepts: The limsup of the nth root of abs(a_n), with the same below-one above-one inconclusive-one trichotomy.
major_error_concepts: Taking an nth root of only part of the term.

cards.prompt: Define Telescoping series. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A series whose partial sums cancel intermediate terms after an explicit decomposition.
required_concepts: A series whose partial sums cancel intermediate terms after an explicit decomposition.
major_error_concepts: Writing cancellation informally without displaying the surviving boundary terms.

cards.prompt: Define Alternating-series approximation error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The next-term error bound for a valid alternating expansion with decreasing magnitudes.
required_concepts: The next-term error bound for a valid alternating expansion with decreasing magnitudes.
major_error_concepts: Using the next-term bound when term magnitudes are not decreasing.

cards.prompt: Define Approximation-order selection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The smallest degree or term count justified to put a remainder below a declared tolerance.
required_concepts: The smallest degree or term count justified to put a remainder below a declared tolerance.
major_error_concepts: Choosing degree from displayed-digit agreement only.

cards.prompt: Define Binomial-series specialization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The power-series expansion of (1+x)^alpha with generalized coefficients on its justified interval and endpoint cases separated.
required_concepts: The power-series expansion of (1+x)^alpha with generalized coefficients on its justified interval and endpoint cases separated.
major_error_concepts: Using ordinary finite binomial coefficients for noninteger alpha and truncating as an identity.

cards.prompt: Define Formal-versus-convergent-series distinction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The separation among a coefficient expression, convergence of the resulting series, and equality to an intended function.
required_concepts: The separation among a coefficient expression, convergence of the resulting series, and equality to an intended function.
major_error_concepts: Calling coefficient agreement at the center proof of function equality nearby.

cards.prompt: Define Geometric power-series representation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The identity 1/(1-x)=sum x^n for abs(x)<1 used as a source for transformed series.
required_concepts: The identity 1/(1-x)=sum x^n for abs(x)<1 used as a source for transformed series.
major_error_concepts: Omitting the interval and claiming equality for x=2.

cards.prompt: Define Interval of convergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The real set including separately adjudicated endpoints in addition to the open radius interval.
required_concepts: The real set including separately adjudicated endpoints in addition to the open radius interval.
major_error_concepts: Assuming that knowing a finite positive convergence radius by itself determines inclusion or exclusion of both real boundary endpoints.

cards.prompt: Define Lagrange remainder. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The Taylor error form f^(n+1)(xi)(x-a)^(n+1)/(n+1)! for some xi between a and x under the theorem hypotheses.
required_concepts: The Taylor error form f^(n+1)(xi)(x-a)^(n+1)/(n+1)! for some xi between a and x under the theorem hypotheses.
major_error_concepts: Evaluating the unknown xi as though it equals x without using a bound.

cards.prompt: State the Maclaurin series for e^x, sin x, cos x, 1/(1-x), and ln(1+x), including their real convergence domains.
cards.definition: The standard Maclaurin series are e^x=sum_{n=0}∞ x^n/n!, sin x=sum_{n=0}∞ (-1)^n x^(2n+1)/(2n+1)!, and cos x=sum_{n=0}∞ (-1)^n x^(2n)/(2n)!, all convergent for every real x. Also 1/(1-x)=sum_{n=0}∞ x^n for |x|<1, and ln(1+x)=sum_{n=1}∞ (-1)^(n+1)x^n/n for -1<x≤1.
required_concepts: State the exponential, sine, and cosine coefficients, powers, and indices; each has infinite radius.
State the geometric series and |x|<1 restriction.
State the logarithm series and its real interval -1<x≤1.
major_error_concepts: sin x=sum_{n=0}∞ x^(2n)/(2n)! and the series for ln(1+x) converges at x=-1.

cards.prompt: Define Power-series algebra. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** addition multiplication scaling and substitution performed only where the participating representations and resulting operations are justified.
required_concepts: addition multiplication scaling and substitution performed only where the participating representations and resulting operations are justified.
major_error_concepts: Claiming that formal series algebra automatically preserves an identity outside justified convergence domains or settles endpoint behavior without analysis.

cards.prompt: Define power-series endpoint test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A power-series endpoint test substitutes each boundary point of the radius interval into the series and tests the resulting numerical series separately for convergence or divergence.
required_concepts: A power-series endpoint test substitutes each boundary point of the radius interval into the series.
Each resulting numerical series is tested separately for convergence or divergence.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the two endpoints have the same convergence behavior or that the radius test settles either endpoint.

cards.prompt: Define Power series. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A function candidate sum c_n(x-a)^n centered at a whose meaning depends on convergence at the chosen x.
required_concepts: A function candidate sum c_n(x-a)^n centered at a whose meaning depends on convergence at the chosen x.
major_error_concepts: Treating x as fixed before identifying the function family.

cards.prompt: Define Radius of convergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The nonnegative radius R for which a power series converges absolutely inside abs(x-a)<R and diverges outside abs(x-a)>R.
required_concepts: The nonnegative radius R for which a power series converges absolutely inside abs(x-a)<R and diverges outside abs(x-a)>R.
major_error_concepts: Including endpoints in the radius conclusion without testing.

cards.prompt: Define Taylor polynomial. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The finite degree-n polynomial using derivatives f^(k)(a)/k! to match local derivative data through order n.
required_concepts: The finite degree-n polynomial using derivatives f^(k)(a)/k! to match local derivative data through order n.
major_error_concepts: Calling the finite polynomial the infinite Taylor series.

cards.prompt: Define Taylor representation criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement that the remainder tends to zero on the claimed domain before the Taylor series is identified with the function.
required_concepts: The requirement that the remainder tends to zero on the claimed domain before the Taylor series is identified with the function.
major_error_concepts: Smoothness alone.

cards.prompt: Define Taylor series. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The formal infinite series sum f^(n)(a)(x-a)^n/n!, whose equality to f requires a remainder or representation argument.
required_concepts: The formal infinite series sum f^(n)(a)(x-a)^n/n!, whose equality to f requires a remainder or representation argument.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every smooth function equals its Taylor series.

cards.term: Termwise differentiation of a power series
cards.prompt: Define Termwise differentiation of a power series. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The differentiated series sum n c_n(x-a)^(n-1) representing the derivative inside the original radius.
required_concepts: The differentiated series sum n c_n(x-a)^(n-1) representing the derivative inside the original radius.
major_error_concepts: Claiming endpoint convergence is unchanged without separate testing.

cards.term: Termwise integration of a power series
cards.prompt: Define Termwise integration of a power series. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integrated series sum c_n(x-a)^(n+1)/(n+1) plus a constant inside the radius.
required_concepts: The integrated series sum c_n(x-a)^(n+1)/(n+1) plus a constant inside the radius.
major_error_concepts: Omitting the constant or representation interval.

cards.prompt: Define Parametric arc length. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of parametric speed over the parameter interval, counting traversal multiplicity.
required_concepts: The integral of parametric speed over the parameter interval, counting traversal multiplicity.
major_error_concepts: Eliminating the parameter and forgetting a repeated traversal.

cards.prompt: Define Parametric area integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The signed area expression integral y dx or related orientation-aware form, converted to parameter with dx/dt.
required_concepts: The signed area expression integral y dx or related orientation-aware form, converted to parameter with dx/dt.
major_error_concepts: Using integral y dt without multiplying by dx/dt in a nontrivial parameterization.

cards.prompt: Define parametrized curve. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A parametrized curve is a mapping from a parameter interval into a geometric space; the parameterization retains orientation, traversal speed, and repeated visits that its image alone does not record.
required_concepts: A parametrized curve is a mapping from a parameter interval into a geometric space
the parameterization retains orientation, traversal speed, and repeated visits that its image alone does not record.
major_error_concepts: Eliminating the parameter and then treating the resulting image as if it preserved orientation, speed, or traversal count.

cards.prompt: Define Parametric first derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** dy/dx=(dy/dt)/(dx/dt) at parameter values where dx/dt is nonzero.
required_concepts: dy/dx=(dy/dt)/(dx/dt) at parameter values where dx/dt is nonzero.
major_error_concepts: Applying dy/dx=(dy/dt)/(dx/dt) at a zero of dx/dt merely because a symbolic factor canceled, without a separate limiting or local-curve argument.

cards.prompt: Define Parametric reparameterization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A new parameter mapping that may preserve the geometric image while changing orientation speed or multiplicity.
required_concepts: A new parameter mapping that may preserve the geometric image while changing orientation speed or multiplicity.
major_error_concepts: Calling equal point sets identical parameterized curves.

cards.prompt: Define Parametric second derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** d/dx(dy/dx)=[d/dt(dy/dx)]/(dx/dt) with all denominator conditions preserved.
required_concepts: d/dx(dy/dx)=[d/dt(dy/dx)]/(dx/dt) with all denominator conditions preserved.
major_error_concepts: Differentiating dy/dx only with respect to t and calling that d2y/dx2.

cards.prompt: Define Parametric self-intersection identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** distinct parameter values mapping to the same point, with slopes and traversal directions audited separately.
required_concepts: distinct parameter values mapping to the same point, with slopes and traversal directions audited separately.
major_error_concepts: Finding one parameter value at the point and assuming a single branch.

cards.prompt: Define Parametric speed. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The nonnegative magnitude sqrt((dx/dt)^2+(dy/dt)^2) retaining parameter-time units.
required_concepts: The nonnegative magnitude sqrt((dx/dt)^2+(dy/dt)^2) retaining parameter-time units.
major_error_concepts: Using dy/dx as speed.

cards.prompt: Define Parametric tangent classification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** horizontal vertical or singular tangent behavior determined from dx/dt and dy/dt together with local curve evidence.
required_concepts: horizontal vertical or singular tangent behavior determined from dx/dt and dy/dt together with local curve evidence.
major_error_concepts: Calling every dx/dt=0 point a vertical tangent even when dy/dt also vanishes.

cards.prompt: Define Polar arc length. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral sqrt(r^2+(dr/dtheta)^2)dtheta over a traversal interval with multiplicity checked.
required_concepts: The integral sqrt(r^2+(dr/dtheta)^2)dtheta over a traversal interval with multiplicity checked.
major_error_concepts: Using the polar area integrand one-half r squared.

cards.prompt: Define Polar area between curves. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The half integral of outer-radius squared minus inner-radius squared over bounds selected from the full intersection audit.
required_concepts: The half integral of outer-radius squared minus inner-radius squared over bounds selected from the full intersection audit.
major_error_concepts: Using (R-r)^2 rather than R^2-r^2.

cards.prompt: Define Polar coordinate representation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The point mapping (r,theta) -> (r cos theta,r sin theta) with nonunique angle and negative-radius representations.
required_concepts: The point mapping (r,theta) -> (r cos theta,r sin theta) with nonunique angle and negative-radius representations.
major_error_concepts: Discarding negative radius as invalid.

cards.prompt: Define Polar intersection search. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The search over nonunique coordinate representations including origin hits and angle shifts, not only equal radii at equal angles.
required_concepts: The search over nonunique coordinate representations including origin hits and angle shifts, not only equal radii at equal angles.
major_error_concepts: Equating radii at one common angle and declaring the list complete.

cards.prompt: Define Polar sector-area differential. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The limiting sector area dA=(1/2)r^2 dtheta underlying polar area formulas.
required_concepts: The limiting sector area dA=(1/2)r^2 dtheta underlying polar area formulas.
major_error_concepts: Using integral r dtheta and obtaining a length-like quantity.

cards.prompt: Define polar symmetry tests.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The substitution tests and geometric reasoning for axis or origin symmetry without treating a passed algebra test as necessary in every representation.
required_concepts: The substitution tests and geometric reasoning for axis or origin symmetry without treating a passed algebra test as necessary in every representation.
major_error_concepts: Using a failed substitution test as proof that no geometric symmetry exists.

cards.prompt: Define Polar tangent slope. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The quotient (r' sin theta+r cos theta)/(r' cos theta-r sin theta) with denominator and simultaneous-zero cases audited.
required_concepts: The quotient (r' sin theta+r cos theta)/(r' cos theta-r sin theta) with denominator and simultaneous-zero cases audited.
major_error_concepts: Using dr/dtheta alone as dy/dx.

description: A definition-recall course deck covering core concepts in Calculus II.
